test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 23 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Yamuna river system?
solution:
The correct answer is __'**Chenab'**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At an elevation of roughly 6387 meters above mean sea level in the district of **Uttarkashi**, the river Yamuna, a significant tributary of the river Ganges, rises from the **Yamunotri glacier** close to the Banderpoonch peaks (380 59' N 780 27' E) in **the Mussoorie range** of the lower Himalayas (Uttaranchal).
 
• The **Himachal Pradesh** and **Jammu and Kashmir** portions of two Indian States are included in the Chenab basin's watershed. In the Himachal Pradesh district of **Chamba**, the Upper Chenab catchment is located in the Lahoul area and Pangi Tehsil.
 
• Therefore, **Chenab** is not a tributary of the Yamuna River system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Tributary** is a little river that empties into a bigger river.
 
• Tons, Chambal, Hindon, Betwa, and Ken are some of the Yamuna River's significant tributaries. The Giri, Sind, Uttangan, Senger, and Rind are additional minor Yamuna River tributaries.
 
• **Hindon:**
 
 
• In India, the Upper **Sivaliks of the Shakumbhari devi** range are where the Hindon River, a **tributary of the Yamuna River**, rises in the** Saharanpur district **of Uttar Pradesh. 
 
• For the rural residents of western Uttar Pradesh, India, it provides a significant supply of freshwater.
 
• The river receives all of its water from rain, and its catchment area is about **7,083 square kilometers **(2,735 sq mi).
 
 
 
• **Sind:**
 
 
• A **tributary of the Yamuna River,** the Sind River traverses the Indian states of **Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh**. 
 
• The Sind runs north-northeast before joining the Yamuna River where it begins on the Malwa plateau in Vidisha, M.P.
 
• It has a drainage area of **27,856 km²** and a total stream network length of **470 kilometers.**
 
 
 
• **Chambal:**
 
 
• In **Central and Northern India**, the Chambal River is a **tributary of the Yamuna River** and is thus a member of the Ganges drainage system. 
 
• The river goes through the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, then turns southeast to join the Yamuna in the state of Uttar Pradesh after briefly passing through Rajasthan and creating the border between the two states.
 
• It is **1,024 kilometers** (636 mi) long.
